OAS recovery tax: keep the income year and deduction calendar separate

Four graphics link a simplified 2025-income recovery calculation with the July 2026 to June 2027 cash period, while keeping ordinary income tax separate.

By TickerLantern Research · Published 25 October 2026 · 4 min read
Sources reviewed 25 October 2026

Change an assumption. Follow the result.

Explore a 2025 OAS recovery illustration and its later cash period

Interactive planning lab

Simplified recovery on 2025 OAS$981.9
New modeled monthly recovery deduction$81.83
Monthly OAS after that deduction only$668.17

Dated 2025-income illustration for an OAS-only Canadian-resident case: 15% of relevant adjusted income above CAD 93,454, capped at entered 2025 OAS. Enter the appropriate income after CRA worksheet adjustments, including OAS where applicable; it is not added again. No GIS/net federal supplements, EI repayment, special adjustments, non-resident tax, ordinary income tax or actual return balance is calculated. The later cash chart holds gross monthly OAS constant from January 2026 through June 2027 and changes the recovery deduction in July 2026. New deduction is the simplified annual recovery divided by twelve, rounded to cents, then capped at monthly gross OAS. Rounding or that cap can make twelve deductions differ from the annual illustration. The cap does not cancel an actual tax obligation. Prior January–June deduction is separately entered and capped at gross. Actual deductions require the Advisory Letter; quarterly pension changes and any approved waiver are not modeled.

The central idea

Label the income year, the benefits received and the later deduction period. An annual recovery estimate and future withholding credits belong to different parts of the tax and cash calendar.

01

Use a threshold for a named income year

Service Canada’s resident OAS repayment explanation uses a CAD 93,454 threshold for 2025 income and a 15% calculation on the excess. This guide fixes that income year instead of silently reusing its threshold for a later year.

The input is the relevant adjusted income for the recovery calculation. The CRA’s line 23500 guidance identifies adjustments to the starting income amount and directs taxpayers to the Federal Worksheet. The tool does not reconstruct those adjustments from account balances or deposits.

Enter the appropriate income including OAS where applicable; do not add the entered pension again. This is an OAS-only Canadian-resident illustration, excluding net federal supplements, EI repayment and non-resident tax. Use the worksheet and actual slips for a return.

02

Calculate the excess, then limit the simplified recovery to the pension

The default relevant 2025 income is CAD 100,000. Subtracting CAD 93,454 leaves CAD 6,546; 15% is CAD 981.90. The example enters CAD 9,000 of gross 2025 OAS.

The model caps recovery at that entered annual pension. The remaining amount is CAD 8,018.10 before ordinary income tax. The cap is for this simplified OAS-only case and is not a substitute for the complete social-benefits repayment calculation.

The income curve holds the selected pension cap fixed and shows the threshold and capped section explicitly. The matrix varies relevant income and pension received. Its hypothetical pension amounts are not official annual maxima or a determination of eligibility, age treatment or residence history.

03

Place the later monthly deduction in its own payment period

The monthly cash chart runs from January 2026 through June 2027. Its first six months use a separately entered prior recovery deduction, which starts at zero in the example. The later illustration begins in July 2026 and runs for twelve months.

To make the cash arithmetic explicit, the tool divides CAD 981.90 by twelve and rounds the monthly planning deduction to cents, giving CAD 81.83. Gross monthly OAS is independently assumed constant at CAD 750. The result after this deduction alone is CAD 668.17.

Twelve deductions at CAD 81.83 total CAD 981.96, six cents more than the annual illustration. Actual deductions follow the Advisory Letter, so the tool does not present its rounding convention as an official payment quote. It also caps a modeled deduction at monthly gross OAS; that display cap does not cancel an actual obligation.

04

Avoid counting later withholding as a second annual recovery charge

The annual bridge concerns benefits received in 2025. The cash chart concerns payments in 2026 and 2027. Its gross monthly amount can differ from the earlier annual pension, so multiplying future monthly cash by twelve will not generally reproduce the annual bridge.

Recovery tax withheld from a pension payment is reported as tax deducted for that payment year. The CRA explains how the amount shown on the slip is claimed with income tax deducted, while the repayment calculation is completed separately.

In this fixed example, the new deduction appears for six months in calendar 2026 and six in 2027, or CAD 490.98 in each calendar year. Do not add all twelve future deductions to CAD 981.90 and label the result the tax on the same 2025 pension. Keep the liability calculation and payment-year credits distinct.

05

Refresh the pension amount and the income estimate separately

The cash chart deliberately holds gross monthly OAS constant to isolate deduction timing. It does not model quarterly pension changes, ordinary income-tax withholding, an age-related increase or a future-year recovery threshold.

If the relevant income changes substantially, the expected deduction based on an earlier year may not match the current situation. The CRA’s line 23500 page describes a request to reduce recovery tax at source when the stated conditions apply. The tool neither submits that request nor assumes approval.

For a working retirement budget, record the Advisory Letter’s effective date and deduction, the gross pension payment and the expected tax-return treatment. Compare those dated amounts with the spending calendar. Use this illustration to understand the moving parts, then replace its assumptions with the confirmed figures.

Sources and scope

Public sources reviewed on 25 October 2026. The OAS graphics are simplified rule-based illustrations using 2025 income and hypothetical benefit amounts. They are not official pension maxima, complete tax calculations or actual Advisory Letter deductions. Original scenario calculations and research checklists are TickerLantern’s educational analysis; attributed publisher examples retain their stated source and scope. Recheck current issuer documents for any product-specific decision.

    Reviewed 25 October 2026. Resident 2025 threshold, illustrative 15% excess-income calculation, later monthly deductions and the Advisory Letter. The source itself directs readers to the Federal Worksheet for their calculation; this article retains that limitation.

  2. CRA · Line 23500: Social benefits repayment ↗

    Reviewed 25 October 2026 for relevant-income adjustments, the distinction between repayment and tax deducted, and the possible request to reduce recovery withholding. No actual tax return, federal supplement or waiver eligibility is computed.
